correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the cited exact density of the ancillary ratio and the exact UMVUE formulas. At the upper endpoint, the estimator is asymptotic to \(c/(1-y)\) while the density is asymptotic to \(K(\alpha)d_0(1-y)^c\), which gives tail index \(p=c+1\) and the displayed constant. The lower endpoint has local moments of every positive order by extending the source proof that \(y^{\beta+1}|G'(y)|\to0\) for every \(\beta>0\). For the rate estimator, independence reduces the problem to a product of the shape-estimator tail and an inverse-Gamma tail. The unequal-index cases use the standard one-heavy-factor product-tail lemma; the equal-index case uses the truncated moment law \(\mathbb E[B^p;B\le t]\sim pC\log t\). The specialization \(q=2\) exactly reproduces the source variance thresholds.

value.rationale: The source highlights finite variance as a fundamental existence property of its new UMVUEs. The finding replaces that single binary threshold with the complete positive-moment spectrum and an exact tail law, and it discovers a distinct parameter transition for the rate estimator between two competing heavy-tail mechanisms, including a logarithmic critical case. These facts directly quantify robustness and the range of loss functions for which risk moments exist, so the invariant is naturally tied to the estimator rather than an arbitrary slice.
